subject: Can I generate data for path model with only observed variables by simulateData function

messages.author: c90f5ebf49405077
messages.subject: Can I generate data for path model with only observed variables by simulateData function
parts: I’m trying to generate data for a path model with 5 observed variables, which include two exogenous variables, two mediators, and one outcome. And I want to generate nonnormal continuous exogenous variables and mediators, and categorical outcome with underlying normal distribution. I have designed the path relationship between them. But now I’m wondering if it is possible to use simulateData function in lavaan package to generate data? I noticed there are only three choices in model.type, which are “cfa”, “sem” and “growth”, and skewness and kurtosis can be apply to all observed variables (all 5 variables in my case, but I only want to apply to 4 of them).

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can I generate data for path model with only observed variables by simulateData function
parts: there are only three choices in model.type, which are “cfa”, “sem” and “growth”

Those are arbitrary.  See the help-page description for what they affect (not the data generation).  Here is an example:

model <- ' # direct effect
             Y ~ .5*X
           # mediator
             M ~ 0.5*X
             Y ~ 0.5*M
           # (residual) variances
             X ~~ 1*X
             M ~~ 0.75*M
             Y ~~ 0.25*Y
'
fitted(sem(model))
simulateData(model, sample.nobs = 5)
skewness and kurtosis can be apply to all observed variables (all 5 variables in my case, but I only want to apply to 4 of them).

So set those to 0 for the fifth variable.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Can I generate data for path model with only observed variables by simulateData function
parts: This is the problem:
>               y | t1 + t2 + t3

You need to specify the values explicitly:

y | -1.2*t1 + 0*t2 + 1.2*t3

An alternative approach is to first generate continuous data, and then
'discretize' y in a second step.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Can I generate data for path model with only observed variables by simulateData function
parts:
On 8/5/20 1:36 AM, Ji Li wrote:
> Hi Dr Rosseel,
>
> Are you suggesting to transfer y into categorical data after applying
> skewness and kurtosis?

Yes. This can be more practical, in particular in the presence of
exogenous covariates.

After the continuous (possibly non-normal) data has been generated, you
can discretize a continuous variable (say, y) as follows: first
standardize y (mean zero, unit variance); then, use the 'cut()' function
with user-specified 'breaks' (=thresholds), eg

y.z <- scale(y)
y.cat <- cut(y.z, breaks = c(-Inf, -1.2, 0, +1.2, +Inf), labels = FALSE)

creates a categorical variable with 4 categories.

Yves.
